fixture.note: The committed pages were rendered with a macOS system font and cannot be reproduced byte for byte on Linux: an exhaustive search over the 1930 fonts on this machine produced no exact match. The generator uses Liberation Sans, which reproduces the page geometry to within four pixels; the recognised text is identical and the model's predicted bounding boxes move by one to three pixels.

single_page.result: PASS: lossless transforms and token ids exact; floating point within 0.002 peak-relative and cosine >= 0.99999 over every checkpoint.

multi_page.note: Same checkpoint family and decoder layer as the exceptions the author retained on macOS (uocr.attention at decoder layers 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8), and the same magnitude (author 0.012268, here 0.010240). The route diagnostics are only in the primitive fixture, which agrees to one or two float32 ULP, so the route flip itself cannot be observed from these traces.

primitive_fixture_drift.note: The official modules recomputed on this machine differ from the committed tests/fixtures/unlimited_ocr_oracle.json by one or two float32 ULP in the rotated rope and the route bias. That is the environment, not the Rust implementation: the fixture holds the official code's own output, and the Rust test tolerance accommodates the difference.

conversions.note: All six formats convert and load. The converter quantises only aligned two-dimensional .weight matrices; convolutions, positions, vectors and unaligned matrices keep the source type, so a quantized export is a mix.

gpu.note: Auto is 2.03 times slower than the CPU on this integrated GPU. The offload threshold is 16384 output elements, so a one-row decode projection stays on the host and only the lm_head reaches the device; with RUST_GPU_MIN_OUTPUTS=0 the submissions rise to 7628 and the output is unchanged. Every device projection is additionally spot-checked against the CPU kernel, the guard added for the flaky device in TODO-044.
